questions.question: The angle of elevation is measured between:
options: The vertical object and the line of sight
The ground and the top of the object
The horizontal through the observer's eye and the upward line of sight
Any two sides of the triangle

questions.question: The angle of depression from a cliff top to a boat equals the angle of elevation from the boat to the cliff top because:
options: The two horizontals are parallel and the line of sight makes equal alternate angles with them
The boat and the cliff are the same height

questions.question: Which situation describes an angle of DEPRESSION?
options: A learner looking up at a flagpole
A boat spotting a lighthouse lamp above
A kite flyer watching the kite climb
A lifeguard on a tower looking down at a swimmer

subtopics.title: The Three-Step Method — Sketch, Label, Choose the Ratio

questions.question: Standing 40 m from a flagpole with elevation 32° to the top, the correct ratio for the height is:
The height of that flagpole, h = 40 tan 32°, is:
Before computing 40 tan 32°, the calculator must be in degree mode because:
options: Degree mode makes the calculator faster
In the wrong mode the ratio value itself is wrong, so every answer after it is wrong

subtopics.title: Finding an Angle and Finding a Distance

questions.question: A 5 m ladder has its foot 2 m from a wall. The angle with the ground satisfies cos θ = 2/5, so θ is:
From a 30 m cliff the angle of depression to a boat is 25°. The boat's distance from the base is:
To find an unknown ANGLE when two sides are known, you must:
options: Use the inverse trig function of the ratio, e.g. θ = cos⁻¹(0,4)
Divide the larger side by the smaller

questions.question: A vertical pole casts a 12 m shadow when the sun's elevation is 55°. The pole's height is:
In a two-observation problem the key strategy is:
options: Average the two angles and use one triangle
Write the shared height from each triangle and equate the two expressions

questions.question: With elevation 38° from A, 50° from B, and B being 20 m closer, the distance d from B to the base satisfies:
Using d ≈ 38,1 m and h = d tan 50°, the tower's height is about:

subtopics.title: Looking Up, Looking Down — Everything Starts Level

questions.question: Every elevation or depression angle is measured starting from:
options: The level horizontal line through the observer's eye

questions.question: A kite flies on 50 m of taut string at an elevation of 40°. Its height is:
You look down at a taxi from a balcony at 35° below your level line. The taxi driver looking up at you sees an elevation of:
options: 35° — the same angle, by alternate angles between parallel level lines
It cannot be found without the height

questions.question: Standing inside the marked angle, the side straight across the triangle from you is the:
In SOH CAH TOA, the TOA part means:
options: The triangle has one right angle

questions.question: If the flagpole observation changes to an elevation of 35° from the same 40 m, the height becomes 40 tan 35°, which is about:

subtopics.title: Reading the Story Into a Sketch

questions.question: The very first move on any worded 2D trig problem is to:
options: Draw the sketch — vertical object, horizontal ground, line of sight

questions.question: In these problems the right angle is found:
options: At the top of the object
Where the vertical object meets the horizontal ground
In the middle of the line of sight

questions.question: The phrase 'from the top of a cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 25°' tells you to draw the 25°:
options: Below a level line drawn through the cliff-top observer
Between the cliff face and the sea
At the boat, above the line of sight
Inside the cliff, at its base
